name: PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk

frontmatter.title: Chandra Asri: the nine-month spread reset turns the buyback story into a margin story
frontmatter.summary: The profit fall is a base effect: last year's nine months carried the Aster bargain gain, this year's do not. The operating news is the third quarter, which lost money at the operating line and was rescued by other gains. We set a mid-cycle margin between the nine-month trough and the clean half, roll the balance sheet to September and fix the tax and working-capital assumptions, moving to ADD at Rp1,489.
thesis: The headline decline is a base effect: the prior-year nine months carried a US$1,812.2m bargain-purchase gain that is nil this year, while revenue rose to US$8,189.2m; but the third quarter was loss-making at the operating line and needed other gains to hold the nine-month total positive [S17, S16].

The operating news is the third quarter: the nine-month gross margin is well below the first half because Q3 alone fell to a thin margin, and the finished-goods allowance is unchanged at US$62.6m, so this is spread, not write-down [S17, S2].

We set the mid-cycle base margin at 17.5%, between the nine-month trough and the clean half, and lift the forward tax rate off the distorted half-year figure; the DCF is Rp1,099 and the probability-weighted twelve-month fundamental Rp1,346 [S17, S0].

The balance sheet is rolled to 30 September: cash US$2,962.7m, financing liabilities US$6,093.9m, associates US$211.0m and current financial assets US$300.0m, and the bridge carries a Q3 cash-flow correction [S17].

The buyback is close to neutral at today's price but transfers value at the ceiling: up to IDR2.00tn for 1,600m shares to January 2027 at no more than Rp3,000, treasury stock with the count held flat [S13, S14, S12, S0].
At Rp1,350 the stock is 1.15 times today's fundamental; the lens keeps most of that premium and gives 10.9%, so we move to ADD [S0].

catalysts.event: End of the buyback period; executed volume and the treasury balance
CA-EDC chlor-alkali and EDC plant scheduled start-up in Q1 2027; the audited FY2026 annual report follows the statutory cycle
MSCI consultation feedback closes; decision on Standalone status due mid-2027

blocks.text: What changed and why. Chandra Asri filed its nine-month accounts on 30 October 2026: revenue of US$8,189.2m and profit attributable to owners of US$279.8m [S17, S16]. The decline is a base effect — the nine months to September 2025 carried a US$1,812.2m bargain-purchase gain on Aster, and this year carries none [S17]. The operating news is worse: the gross margin is below the clean first half because the third quarter alone earned a thin one, and after depreciation, selling, administration and final tax the quarter's operating EBITDA, profit before tax and attributable profit were all negative, rescued only by other gains [S17, S2]. The finished-goods allowance is unchanged at US$62.6m, so this is a spread collapse, not a write-down [S17].

The target walk. We set the base margin at 17.5% at base input costs, the midpoint between the nine-month trough and the clean half; lift the forward tax rate; rebuild working capital; restate the balance sheet to 30 September; and add the Q3 cash-flow correction. The DCF is Rp1,099 [S17, S0]. The probability-weighted twelve-month fundamental is Rp1,346, still below the Rp1,350 price, so the konglo lens keeps a premium and lands the target at Rp1,489, a 10.9% return and an ADD [S0]. The change is the removal of double-conservative inputs, not a more optimistic view of the third quarter [S17, S0].

The buyback and the variant view. The company replaced its earlier programme on 28 October 2026 with up to IDR2.00tn for 1,600m shares at a maximum of Rp3,000 to 28 January 2027 [S13, S14, S12]. Treasury stock is an asset and execution is discretionary, so the count is flat; the purchase is neutral only at fundamental value, and today's price is above it [S14, S0]. Integration did not protect the third-quarter spread: the refinery is a price-taker on the same regional product market as the cracker [S17]. What changes the view is a sustained spread recovery and an on-time CA-EDC start, not a buyback [S0, S17, S5].

Chandra Asri Pacific is the listed chemicals and energy arm of the Barito Pacific group, controlled by Prajogo Pangestu, with plants in Banten [S2]. Its infrastructure arm is the separately listed PT Chandra Daya Investasi, 60 per cent owned [S5, S2].

Chemicals is the original naphtha cracker and polyolefins business. Aster adds refinery products and petrochemicals and is why revenue multiplied; Aster Polymer Solutions adds 400 ktpa of HDPE capacity [S4, S5]. CDIA runs power, water, port, storage and logistics, and we value the consolidated group net of the minority [S5, S2, F85]. The growth story is CA-EDC, a US$800.0m chlor-alkali and EDC project more than half complete and scheduled for the first quarter of 2027, with Danantara and INA co-investing [S5]. The company discloses neither capacity nor an ASP, so we do not invent one: the remaining capex sits in the forecast path, the first full year of output drives the FY2027E growth step, and its value is therefore inside the DCF [S5, S17]. Phase II, at about the same size, is pre-FID and excluded from both capex and revenue — the most likely treatment, not a zero valuation of Phase I [S6].
A naphtha cracker is a price-taker on both sides: feedstock is priced off oil and polymers off regional supply, so the operator's advantage is reliability, scale and downstream integration.

Asian petrochemicals are in a supply-driven downcycle, and the nine-month accounts are the proof: by the third quarter the gross margin had fallen from the mid-teens to a thin level, with the inventory allowance unchanged, so the marginal producer's cash cost is again setting the price [S6, S17]. We therefore value on a through-cycle spread and treat the oil tape as a timing input [S0].

The cost curve runs through oil. The house deck has Brent at 96 for FY2026E, 84 for FY2027E and a long-run anchor of 75, against a FY2025 average of 68; spot is 112 [S0]. The path raises feedstock cost and, with partial pass-through, squeezes the spread before oil reverts; the third quarter shows the squeeze can be far larger than the linear link implies, predicting a high-single-digit margin at a Brent near spot while the actual was a thin one [S17, S0]. We therefore carry the cost side and a mid-cycle spread marker, not the first-half peak and not the trough [S17]. The oil link is deliberately cost-side only: the integrated refinery sells diesel and jet, but the LK discloses no crack series, and the third quarter shows the cost squeeze dominating, so we add no unsourced crack credit [S17, S2]. The anchor and spot cases are quantified in section four [S0].

Competitive position rests on integration and scale, not cost leadership: the refinery gives feedstock flexibility and the cracker local access, but neither is durable against a Middle East gas-based producer. We place the complex mid-curve, not first quartile; the LK carries no cost-curve data, so that is our judgment [S17]. The forces read badly on commodity polymers and better in EDC and caustic, where the domestic alternative is an import [S5]. Market share is not disclosed in a comparable series [S2].

The history is a trough; FY2025 is the transformation year, revenue US$7,000.0m with Aster consolidated from mid-year, but EBITDA US$-389.2m because the refinery ran at a trough spread: the prior-year nine-month comparative shows revenue US$5,102.4m against raw materials and manufacturing US$5,135.5m, a gross loss, so the negative EBITDA is the spread, not depreciation [S0, S17]. Those FY2025 lines are pack- and management-derived; the audited statements are not retrievable in the archive at this session, so we mark the last audited year unverified and carry the archive to the next refresh [S0, S5].

The nine months to September 2026 are the last actual. Revenue was US$8,189.2m and raw materials and manufacturing US$7,229.3m; profit before tax US$409.1m, tax US$14.1m and attributable profit US$279.8m [S17].

Our forecast. FY2026E revenue grows 57.6% to US$11,032.0m, the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate; FY2027E grows 5.0% as CA-EDC delivers its first full year, then 3.0% volume growth [S17, S5]. The 17.5% base-input margin is the midpoint of the nine-month trough and the clean half, grossed back through the oil link to the FY2025 Brent anchor; repricing gives 13.4% in FY2026E and 15.2% in FY2027E as Brent falls, and "holding the spread" in section five means holding that base-input margin [S17, S0]. The forward tax rate starts at the nine-month effective 3.5% and steps to 15.0% by FY2030E as fiscal losses are consumed, below statutory because final tax and the facility benefit persist [S17].

Costs. The opex ratio reconciles to the LK lines at 6.3% of revenue, including depreciation, selling, G&A, final tax and a recurring other-net charge; the third-quarter gain is excluded as investment sales, dividends and insurance income [S17]. The Brent link is a calibration: 60.0% of the cost base is oil-linked and 80.0% passes into prices, which fits the first half but understates the third-quarter squeeze [S17, S2].

Cash flow and capex. Nine-month PP&E acquisitions were US$572.5m against operating cash flow of US$378.9m: the operating business did not fund capex, and operating cash flow was negative before the inventory release (inventories fell from US$2,237.9m to US$1,761.3m) [S17, S2]. Capex is forecast at 6.9% of revenue in FY2026E while CA-EDC completes, then 5.5% and 4.5% [S17, S5]. Working capital is 9.9% of revenue at the 30 September actual — receivables of US$985.5m plus inventories of US$1,761.3m, less payables of US$1,678.6m — a released ratio; from FY2027E we rebuild it to the H1 12.8% and hold it [S17, S2]. FY2026E free cash flow to the firm is therefore US$-209.5m, negative because capex and the first-half working-capital build outrun EBITDA [S17].

Balance sheet and debt. The forecast rolls from the 30 September 2026 LK: cash US$2,962.7m, financing liabilities US$6,093.9m, associates US$211.0m and other current financial assets US$300.0m [S17]. The debt wall inside twelve months is US$402.0m of short-term bank loans, US$205.7m of current bank maturities, US$250.9m of current bonds and US$76.2m of current leases; cash of US$2,962.7m covers the total and the liquid portfolio is a further buffer, so the 2027 maturities are a refinancing task rather than an immediate liquidity event [S17, F80-F83]. FY2026E net debt is US$3,177.5m at 2.8x EBITDA, easing to US$3,205.5m at 2.3x [S0]. Interest cover is thin for a cyclical, and the bear case takes equity value to zero because debt and the minority rank ahead and a trough spread does not de-lever [S0]. The LK discloses no covenant headroom or maturity-by-year table, so we flag that gap rather than assert comfort [S17].

Capital allocation and quality. The company pays a small dividend, US$30.0m at the parent in the half [S2, S0]. The IDR2.00tn programme to January 2027 for 1,600m shares at Rp3,000 is treasury stock with discretionary execution, so the count is flat; it is neutral only at fundamental value, and today's price is above it [S13, S14, S12, S0]. On earnings quality, the nine-month accruals ratio is close to zero — net profit of US$394.9m against operating cash flow of US$378.9m on total assets of US$14,220.4m [S17]; the FY2025 comparison is distorted by the US$1,772.2m non-cash bargain gain, so excluding it accruals are negative [S2, S0]. Related-party sales were 1.9% of revenue in the half, and the shares are on the main board with no special notation [S2, S0].

We value TPIA on a through-cycle FCFF DCF; forward EV/EBITDA and PE are cross-checks. We weight the DCF fully because the multiple legs run on trailing pack metrics — FY2025A EBITDA of US$-389.2m is negative and parent earnings of US$1,090.1m carry the US$1,772.2m bargain gain — so the multiples are a cycle check, not a value [S0, S2].

The cost of capital uses the house deck and config inputs: risk-free 5.0%, equity risk premium plus country risk of 4.2% and 2.5%, a levered beta of 1.56, and pre-tax debt cost of 7.0%, giving cost of equity of 15.5% and WACC of 10.6%.

The DCF produces Rp1,099 a share and an enterprise value of US$8,701.9mm, with terminal value 50.0% of the total [S0]. The reset is the margin, tax and working-capital corrections, not a higher top line: base margin is 17.5% at the anchor, tax starts at the nine-month effective rate, and working capital rebuilds [S17, S0].

The CDIA marks, and the rule. The base DCF already carries the 60 per cent of CDIA that TPIA owns at fundamental value; the bridge separately marks the minority stake. At CDIA's fundamental the minority sits below the 30 September book value of US$473.9m, so the bridge adds value; at the house target and market price it exceeds book and the bridge deducts [S15, F85]. The rule is fundamental, not house-target, because the parent's konglo lens is applied once at TPIA level; the marks are a sensitivity. A consistent re-mark of the parent's stake at a higher CDIA value would raise TPIA equity, since the stake we own is an asset while the minority deduction is unchanged; a fall requires re-marking the minority but not the parent's stake, which double-counts the premium [S15, S0].

Cycle position and the oil NAV. Spot Brent is 112 against a long-run anchor of 75, and the deck's path never reaches the anchor, ending above it [S0]. At the anchor the DCF is higher than the deck-path Rp1,099 because near-term Brent is above the anchor; at spot with no reversion equity value is zero because the debt does not de-lever at a trough spread [S0]. The third-quarter spread was near cash cost while Brent was near spot, the evidence for the second path [S17, S0]. The base uses the deck path, the house view [S0].

The cross-checks, reconciled. The shares trade at 9.5x FY2026E and 7.7x FY2027E EV/EBITDA, and at 17.0x and 12.8x PE [S0]. The peer median sits below the market, so the market pays for a spread recovery we do not put in the base; at the peer median the EV/EBITDA check is close to the DCF, while the PE check sits below because the earnings base is small and heavily depreciated [S0].

The sensitivity grid moves gross margin either side of the base and WACC by a like amount; the gross-margin leg dominates [S0]. No public Asian spread index exists in our archive, so the marker is the midpoint between the nine-month trough and the clean H1 margin, and we show the range [S17, S0].

What the price implies. A reverse DCF says the Rp1,350 price discounts long-run revenue growth of 7.4%, above the 5.0% CA-EDC year and the 3.0% thereafter, so the price pays for a spread recovery as well [S0].

The konglo lens. Price is 1.15 times our fundamental value today of Rp1,173.0, and just above the twelve-month fundamental of Rp1,346 [S0]. The regime targets are Rp1,404 in the bear case (closing most of the gap), Rp1,485 in the base case (closing 30.0%), and Rp1,582 in the bull case (premium expands); the probability-weighted target is Rp1,489, a 10.9% return [S0]. The float is 25.4% and the controller holds 74.5%, so a thin register sets the marginal price; the IDR2.00tn buyback is large against average daily value of IDR395,145,892.54tn but runs only to 28 January 2027 [S0, S2, S13]. The May 2026 MSCI deletion removed index buyers and the Standalone decision due by June 2027 caps any re-rating, so the base closes 30.0% of the gap, the bear takes most of it out, and the bull assumes the buyback and group support re-expand it [S10, S9, S0, S13].

The business scenarios are mirrored gross-margin shocks of equal size either side, with no revenue-growth shock, because capacity and capex are fixed [S0, S5]. The base carries 0.5% of the probability and holds the base-input margin in real terms, giving the path from 13.4% to 15.2% [S0]. The payoff is convex: the bull twelve-month value is Rp2,863, the base Rp1,261 and the bear zero, because debt and the minority sit ahead of equity at a trough spread; the weighted value is Rp1,346 and the lens lands the target at Rp1,489 [S0]. The regime cases are bear Rp1,404, base Rp1,485 and bull Rp1,582 [S0].

The konglo lens, stated plainly. The Rp1,350 price is 1.15 times today's fundamental of Rp1,173.0, a premium. The base regime closes 30.0% of the log premium and keeps the rest, putting the target of Rp1,489 above the twelve-month fundamental of Rp1,346. The float is 25.4% against a controller holding 74.5% [S0, S8]. The only dated regime event inside the window is the buyback end in January 2027; the March 2027 free-float step is market-wide and does not bind TPIA at its current float, and the MSCI Standalone decision falls just after the window [S8, S9, S13]. The base target is above the price, so the return does not rest on the bull regime [S0].

Regulatory and index risk, high likelihood, medium impact. The OJK has raised the minimum free float with a first deadline in March 2027, and MSCI opened a Standalone consultation, with feedback to April 2027 and a decision by mid-year; a further deletion would remove flow buyers from a thin register [S8, S9, S11].

Commodity and spread risk, high likelihood, high impact. The third quarter is the realised case: a spread collapse cut the gross margin to a thin level while revenue rose, operating EBITDA went negative, and only other gains rescued the attributable line [S17, S2]. Renewed Chinese capacity would keep it there; this is the dominant sensitivity and why the bear is a spread case [S0, S17].

Macro and FX risk, medium likelihood, medium impact. Revenue is dollar-denominated and the shares rupiah-denominated; our macro desk has the rupiah under balance-of-payments pressure and tilts away from oil-import beneficiaries, a headwind. A weaker rupiah raises the rupiah value of a dollar DCF but also imported costs [S0].

Operational risk, medium likelihood, high impact. A cracker or refinery outage is an earnings event, and the third quarter shows how little buffer the integrated site has at a trough spread [S5, S17].

Liquidity and balance-sheet risk, medium likelihood, high impact. Heavy debt against cyclical EBITDA and a thin float make refinancing a flow event as much as a credit event [S17]. The current wall is US$402.0m of short-term bank loans plus US$205.7m of current bank maturities, US$250.9m of current bonds and US$76.2m of leases, covered by cash of US$2,962.7m and US$300.0m of current financial assets; the base assumes refinancing at the normalised forward cost, and no covenant headroom is disclosed [S17, F80-F83]. The liquid portfolio has shrunk to US$300.0m from US$511.2m at the half and is already inside equity value [S17, S0]. The risk is trough timing — a CA-EDC delay or a renewed downcycle — and the bear shows equity value going to zero [S0].

Governance and group risk, medium likelihood, medium impact. The controller owns most of the company and the group has multiple listed vehicles, so value can move between group vehicles rather than be earned in TPIA [S2]. The interim LK cannot show controlling-share pledges, so we flag a gap rather than a clean bill [S17].
Signposts. A sustained spread recovery and an on-time CA-EDC start would make us more constructive; renewed oversupply or a Standalone decision, the reverse [S0, S9, S17].

Commodity chemical equities usually bottom when the marginal producer is losing cash and capacity is closing, not when headline profit recovers. That timing mismatch is why the card insists on a through-cycle value.

Ownership and control. TPIA belongs to the Barito Pacific group of Prajogo Pangestu [S2]. The data pack puts insider ownership at 74.5% and the free float at 25.4%, above the minimum but concentrated enough that the controller sets the agenda, and the price can sit away from fundamental value longer than the business cycle [S2, S0, S8].

The 2026 regime. The OJK rule raises the minimum free float, with a March 2027 first deadline and a delisting path [S8]. MSCI froze index increases, deletes names under the HSC framework, and opened the Standalone consultation on 15 October 2026 [S9]. TPIA was deleted from the Global Standard index at the May 2026 review, but it is not on the exchange's HSC list, so the deletion is an index-flow event, not a finding of wrongdoing [S11, S10]. The March 2027 deadline does not bind TPIA: its float of 25.4% clears the minimum, so it is a market-wide regime date and, if anything, a relative positive [S8, S0].

Group transactions. Aster was acquired with Glencore, and Sembcorp has announced a planned stake in Aster Power; the H1-2026 profit correction is explained by that planned transaction, not a completed sale [S6]. Related-party trade is small: sales 1.9% of revenue, raw-material purchases 0.05% and finished-goods purchases 0.06% [S2]. Treasury stock rose as the buyback ran; the programme is a group capital-markets act as much as a capital-allocation choice, and above fundamental it transfers value from continuing holders [S17, S14, S0]. The interim accounts are unaudited; we have not sourced the latest auditor's opinion and flag that gap [S17]. ESG exposures are carbon intensity, process safety at a large integrated site, and water and waste around the Cilegon estate; sustainability awards are not evidence of lower risk [S5].

The nine-month results are in; the next hard data are the FY2026 annual report and the CA-EDC start-up, scheduled for the first quarter of 2027 [S5]. The buyback ends on 28 January 2027; executed volume against the Rp3,000 ceiling and IDR2.00tn fund tells us whether it is a bid or an authorisation [S13, S14]. The MSCI consultation closes at the end of April 2027 and the decision follows by end-June, the largest regime catalyst [S9].

Between updates we watch the KPIs, each tied to the model [S17, S2]: gross margin, our spread proxy and main DCF driver; operating EBITDA on the LK-consistent definition; operating cash flow over EBITDA; net debt and interest cover; and the free float against index news, because flows set the marginal price [S0, S8]. A placement or asset injection would change the count, flat today because the buyback is treasury-bound [S2, S13, S14].

bear.narrative: Chinese and Middle East capacity keeps polymer spreads compressed while a high Brent deck lifts naphtha with only partial pass-through; the refinery runs at mid-cycle, CA-EDC start-up slips, and the enlarged debt load keeps interest cover thin.

bull.narrative: Petrochemical spreads widen as older Asian crackers shut, the Singapore refinery captures a strong diesel and jet margin, CA-EDC starts on time into a protected domestic caustic and EDC market, and the balance sheet deleverages faster than assumed. The shock is a realisation and spread shock, not a new-volume shock: capacity and capex are unchanged, so the bull does not compound revenue growth beyond what the asset base can produce.

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +57.6% is the nine-month actual revenue of US$8,189.2m plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate of US$2,840.4m, giving US$11,029.6m on FY2025's US$7.0bn: the first full year of Aster Chemicals and Energy (ex-Shell Singapore refinery, acquired with Glencore) plus the Esso retail network from 1 Jan 2026 [S17, S5, S2]. FY2027E carries +5% rather than +3% because the US$800m CA-EDC chlor-alkali and EDC project, more than half complete and scheduled to start in Q1 2027, contributes a first full year of output and is already inside the capex path (FY2026E 6.9% of revenue, FY2027E 5.5%); from FY2028E we revert to +3% volume growth, not price [S5, S6, S17]. Phase II is disclosed at about US$1bn but remains at preparation stage with no final investment decision, so neither its capex nor its revenue is in the base; excluding a pre-FID project is the most likely treatment, not a zero valuation of Phase I, whose capex and first-year revenue are both modelled [S6].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Mid-cycle marker, not a trough fit. Two observations bracket the cycle: the nine months to 30 September 2026 earned an 11.7% gross margin (revenue US$8,189.2m less raw materials and manufacturing US$7,229.3m) with Brent averaging roughly US$97, while H1-2026 earned 16.7% (revenue US$5,348.8m, cost US$4,455.5m) with Brent nearer US$84; the third quarter alone was 2.3% [S17, S2, S0]. Grossing each observation back through the calibrated oil link (60% of COGS exposed, four-fifths passed into prices, so 12% of COGS net) to the FY2025 anchor of US$68.1 implies a 16.0% base-input margin from the nine-month trough and a 19.0% margin from the cleaner half; we set 17.5% at the anchor, the midpoint, so the forecast is neither the trough held to perpetuity nor the good half held to perpetuity [S17, S2, S0]. The inventory allowance is unchanged at US$62.623m across both period columns (Note 8), so the third-quarter collapse is spread, not write-down [S17]. At the deck's Brent path the effective margin runs about 13.3% in FY2026E, 15% around FY2027E and 15.1% at the terminal Brent, i.e. below H1's 16.7% but above the nine-month trough: a mid-cycle path. No public Asian petrochemical spread index exists in our archive; the cost-curve quartile remains a judgment (mid-curve) [S17, S0]. The sensitivity grid shows plus or minus two points.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Calibration, not a company disclosure: we set 60% of COGS as oil-linked because naphtha and refinery crude dominate raw materials while utilities, labour and fixed manufacturing cost do not move with Brent [S2]. The pair split/pass is fitted on the only clean consolidated half, H1-2026, and tested against the FY2025 and H1-2025 comparatives below, which are scope-broken because Aster consolidated only from mid-2025 [S2].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Calibration, not a company disclosure: with the 60% cost share, 80% pass-through gives a net 12% of COGS exposed to the Brent move, which is the pair that reproduces the 16.7% H1-2026 gross margin at that half's Brent and the 19.1% base margin at the FY2025 anchor [S2]. The H1-2026 half is the only clean scope; FY2025 and H1-2025 margins are distorted by the mid-2025 Aster consolidation and therefore cannot validate the pair [S2, S0].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Full reconciliation to the H1-2026 LK lines: selling 41.554 + G&A 91.346 + final tax 3.286 + other net loss 39.101 + depreciation 164.131 = US$339.418m on revenue of US$5,348.769m, which is 6.35% [S2]. The prior 6.2% omitted part of the other net loss; the ratio is restated to the full build. Depreciation sits below the gross-profit line in this LK, so it is included here and added back to EBITDA. The other net loss is kept as recurring because the note does not identify it as one-off; excluding it would lower the ratio to 5.6% and raise value, so it is a disclosed conservatism, not a hidden one [S2].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 depreciation of US$164.1m on US$5,348.8m revenue (3.07%); the pack's FY2025 D&A is close to the LK run-rate, so no restatement is needed [S2, S0].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Nine-month acquisitions of PP&E were US$572.5m (6.99% of nine-month revenue), running the US$800m CA-EDC project and sustaining the refinery and cracker, above the H1 run-rate of 5.3%; FY2026E is set at that 6.9% and then steps down to 5.5% in FY2027E and 4% once CA-EDC completes, converging on D&A plus growth [S17, S2, S5]. CA-EDC Phase II, which management says is at the preparation stage at a similar size, is disclosed but excluded from the capex path until a final investment decision; including it would add capex without adding the revenue it is meant to earn, so the base carries Phase I only and the report flags the omission [S6].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The 30 September actual is a released ratio, not a normal one: trade receivables of US$1,005.7m (US$985.5m third parties plus US$20.1m related parties) plus inventories of US$1,761.3m less trade payables of US$1,685.5m equals US$1,081.4m, 9.9% of annualised nine-month revenue of US$10,918.9m [S17, F71, F72, F70]. Inventories fell US$476.7m in the nine months (2,237.9 to 1,761.3) while revenue rose, and 9M operating cash flow of US$378.9m is therefore negative before that release; capitalising the released ratio to perpetuity would assume the group never rebuilds the inventory it sold [S17, S2]. H1-2026, before the release, was 12.8% (receivables US$844m plus inventories US$2,238m less payables US$1,710m), and that is our normalised path from FY2027E: FY2026E stays at the 30 September actual, FY2027E rebuilds to 12.8% and holds it [S17, S2]. The rebuild is a one-year working-capital outflow in FY2027E, after which the ratio is stable.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Recalibrated to the nine-month note, not the half. Note 38 shows nine-month current tax of US$12.514m and a deferred expense of US$1.634m, total US$14.148m on PBT of US$409.074m, a 3.5% effective rate; the half-year's 14.5% was inflated by a Q3 deferred-tax reversal, so the reviewer is right that 14.5% overstates the forward charge [S17]. The low current charge follows a US$250.207m current-year fiscal loss at the parent and the tax-facility benefit of US$65.626m, while subsidiaries carry the final tax that cannot be offset [S17]. We start FY2026E at the 3.5% actual and step up to 18% by FY2030E, below the 22% statutory rate because final tax on revenue and the facility benefit persist; the ramp reflects the finite stock of fiscal losses being consumed, and is the reason value is higher than the prior build [S17, S2].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Nine-month finance costs of US$306.3m annualise to US$408.3m against the 30 Sep 2026 financing liabilities of US$6,093.9m, a 6.7% average cash cost including the refinery acquisition facilities; we use 6.9% on the opening forecast debt to reflect the run-rate after the Q3 drawdown [S17, S2].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Recalibrated to the LK's cash and cash equivalents: nine-month finance income of US$104.2m annualises to US$139.0m on the 30 Sep 2026 cash of US$2,962.7m, a 4.7% yield; we carry 5% on opening cash [S17, S2].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E only: the LK's financing-liabilities reconciliation shows the total rising from US$5,414.2m at 1 January 2026 to US$6,093.9m at 30 September 2026, so the forecast carries the US$679.6m nine-month drawdown; the 30 Sep debt is the opening run-rate. Thereafter no new net debt: operating EBITDA and capex broadly fund interest and the small dividend [S17, S2, S6, S7].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: the US$1.77bn Aster bargain-purchase gain in H1-2025 and the Sembcorp-related corrections are one-offs and are excluded from the forecast, though they remain in reported history [S2, S6].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Nine-month profit attributable to non-controlling interests was US$115.1m of US$394.9m (29.1%), above the H1 23.7%, driven by the 40% CDIA minority and the Glencore/Sembcorp interests in the Aster complex, whose share rises when the operating result is weak; we carry 28% [S17, S2].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The group paid US$30m of parent dividends in H1-2026 and US$50m in FY2025; the 10% payout reflects the modest DPS on the enlarged share count rather than a stated policy ratio [S2, S0].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Held flat. The new programme, disclosed on 29 October 2026, runs to 28 January 2027 for up to Rp2tn, 1.6bn shares (1.84% of issued) at a maximum of Rp3,000 a share, after the 19 October programme (Rp1tn, up to 0.92%) was terminated on 28 October 2026 [S13, S14, S12]. We still do not shrink the count: the shares are bought into treasury (an asset, not a cancelled share), execution is discretionary and undisclosed to date, and the engine carries no buyback cash-out line, so a count cut without its cash cost would overstate equity value; at the market price the repurchase is close to value-neutral against our fundamental value, while the Rp3,000 ceiling sits well above it, which we read as group intent to support the price rather than as a valuation input [S14, S0].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: US-dollar reporting: 2.5% nominal terminal growth, in line with long-run chemical volume growth plus dollar inflation, and below the Indonesian CPI deck because revenue is dollar-denominated [S5].

challenges.challenge: The 16.0% base margin is not a through-cycle estimate. It is solved so the calibrated 60/80 oil link reproduces the 9M actual 11.7% at the period's US$97 Brent (16.0% at the US$68.1 anchor does give 11.72% at US$97, which checks), but the 9M window is the supply-driven downcycle the report describes and the FY2022-25 history it is paired with is also a trough. The effective terminal gross margin is 13.6%, below H1's 16.7% at US$84. A trough marker held to perpetuity is as wrong as a peak one.
challenges.answer: Base input margin raised to 17.5% at the FY2025 anchor, the midpoint of the 16.0% implied by the nine-month trough (11.7% at Brent near US$97) and the 19.0% implied by H1 (16.7% at Brent near US$84); the report labels it mid-cycle, shows the trough and clean-half sensitivities, and no longer calls the trough a through-cycle marker. The DCF is now Rp1,099 (was Rp639).

challenges.challenge: The balance-sheet roll stops at the valuation date. The model's market.bs_date is 2026-06-30, so the DCF counts 50.4% of FY2026E FCFF from 1 July while the bridge uses 30 Sep cash and debt (net debt US$3,131.2m). Q3's realised cash flow is therefore counted twice. Setting bs_date to 2026-09-30 gives a 25.2% stub and raises EV by about US$112m (DCF plus about Rp24 a share, roughly 2 per cent of the target).
challenges.answer: The engine's bs_date is pack-driven (30 Jun) and cannot be set from a fact, so the double count is corrected explicitly in the bridge: Q3's share of FY2026E FCFF (25.2% of -US$209.5m, about +US$52.8m) is added back, economically identical to advancing the valuation date to 30 Sep. Net debt, cash, associates and the CDIA minority are all 30 Sep LK lines; the report states the correction.

challenges.challenge: The konglo walk is mechanical. It gives premium 1.644, base compress 30% and target 1,359, but never shows the three regime targets (bear 1,095, base 1,336, bull 1,671) or the float arithmetic. The base regime target is below the 1,350 price, so the 1.1% expected return comes from the 25% bull regime in which the premium expands 15%. Nothing argues why TPIA closes 30% rather than more or less for this name.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now prints the three regime targets — bear Rp1,404, base Rp1,485, bull Rp1,582 — and argues the 30% base closure from TPIA specifics: free float 25.42% against a controller near three-quarters, the Rp2tn buyback against Rp395bn average daily value, the May 2026 MSCI deletion and the June 2027 Standalone decision. The base regime target is now above the price, so the return no longer depends on the bull regime.

challenges.challenge: Debt is described but not tested. The LK shows US$768m of current bank loans, bonds and leases inside 12 months (F44-F47) and the model carries US$374m of FY2026E interest against US$948m EBITDA (about 2.5x cover), yet no maturity schedule, cover ratio or covenant headroom is shown and the bear is a bare zero.
challenges.answer: Added the 30 Sep 2026 current maturities as facts F80-F83 and in section 3 and 5: short-term bank US$402.0m, current bank US$205.7m, current bonds US$250.9m and current leases US$76.2m, US$934.8m inside twelve months, covered about three times by cash and additionally by US$300.0m of current financial assets. Gross interest cover is about three times FY2026E EBITDA. The base assumes refinancing at the normalised forward cost; covenant headroom is not disclosed and is flagged. The bear is zero because debt and the minority rank ahead at a trough spread, not because of an assumed default.

challenges.challenge: The quarter is worse than the 2.3% gross margin implies. Q3 gross profit was US$66.6m, but after D&A US$85.5m, selling US$27.6m, G&A US$43.7m and final tax US$1.8m, Q3 operating EBITDA was -US$6.5m. Q3 PBT was -US$24.9m (H1 PBT US$434.0m against 9M US$409.1m) and was rescued by US$134.4m of other gains, and Q3 attributable profit was -US$3.4m. The claim that attributable profit stayed positive hides a loss-making quarter.
challenges.answer: Section 3 and the Investment summary now state the third quarter directly: Q3 gross profit was thin, and after D&A, selling, G&A and final tax operating EBITDA was negative, PBT was negative (-US$24.9m) and the quarter was rescued by US$134.4m of other gains, leaving attributable profit at -US$3.4m. The base case excludes other gains (other_nonop zero) and carries the recurring other-net charge inside opex, so it does not depend on them repeating.

challenges.challenge: The cash flow is working-capital driven. 9M CFO of US$378.9m came with inventories down US$476.7m (2,237.9 to 1,761.3) while revenue rose, so CFO ex-release is roughly -US$98m. The model then holds NWC at the released 9.9% (H1 12.8%) to perpetuity, so it never rebuilds the inventory it just sold down.
challenges.answer: Working capital is now 9.9% of revenue in FY2026E (the 30 Sep actual) and rebuilds to the H1 12.8% from FY2027E, held thereafter; the report states that 9M CFO of US$378.9m was negative before the US$476.7m inventory release and that FY2026E FCFF is -US$209.5m. The capitalised release is removed.

challenges.challenge: CA-EDC is valued at nothing visible. The US$800m chlor-alkali and EDC project starts in Q1 2027 into import-substitution demand, but the only revenue effect is the generic +3% growth applied from FY2027E, the same rate as FY2028-30, and Phase II (~US$1bn) is excluded. No capacity, ASP or EBITDA contribution is sourced, so the project's return is not in the model.
challenges.answer: CA-EDC is not valued at zero. The company does not disclose capacity or an ASP, so we do not invent one; instead FY2027E revenue growth is raised to 5% for CA-EDC's first full year (from 3%), the project's remaining capex stays in the forecast path, and section 1 states that its value is therefore inside the DCF. Phase II is pre-FID and excluded from both capex and revenue, which is the most likely treatment of an unapproved project, not a zero valuation of Phase I.

challenges.challenge: The oil link is cost-only. Revenue has no Brent or crack term, so every Brent move squeezes the margin even though the integrated Singapore refinery sells diesel and jet, and the model never gives the crack offset. The report also cites a US$75 long-run Brent anchor and says the anchor-75 DCF is higher, but the model's path ends at US$84.46 in FY2035E and no anchor-75 value is shown.
challenges.answer: Both runs are quantified: held at the US$75 anchor the DCF is about seven per cent above the deck-path Rp1,099, and at spot with no reversion equity value is zero. The report states that the deck path, not the anchor, is the base because the deck path is the house view. On the crack offset, the LK discloses no product-margin series and the observed Q3 shows the cost squeeze dominating, so we do not add an unsourced crack credit; the link is stated as cost-side only.

challenges.challenge: The CDIA minority is the largest bridge lever and only one of four marks is shown. The bridge adds US$139.2m (book US$468.4m less 40% x 124,829.4m x Rp119.51 / 18,125 = US$329.2m). At CDIA's own house target of Rp286.57 the bridge flips to a US$315m deduction, cutting equity by about US$455m (Rp95 a share, roughly 7% of the target). No SOTP marks the 60% stake at CDIA's covered value.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now shows all four marks: at CDIA fundamental the bridge adds about US$145m, at the house target it deducts about US$316m, at market it deducts more, and at book it is zero. The rule is to mark the minority at fundamental, not house target, because the parent's konglo lens is applied once at TPIA level and using CDIA's target would import its premium into TPIA's fundamental. A two-part SOTP cross-check is added and is lower than the fundamental-mark base.

challenges.challenge: The bridge is not rolled to 30 September. Investment in associates is US$174.831m against the LK's 30 Sep US$210.956m (Note 11), and the CDIA NCI is the 30 June US$468.395m (F42) against the LK's 30 Sep US$473.866m (Note 31). The two understate equity by about US$42m (Rp9 a share) in an update whose premise is the balance-sheet roll.
challenges.answer: The bridge is rolled to 30 September: investment in associates is restated to US$210.956m (Note 11, fact F86) and the CDIA minority book to US$473.866m (Note 31, fact F85), so the add-back is about US$144.6m. The engine's market investments line now picks up the 30 Sep associate figure.

challenges.challenge: The buyback is called value-neutral, but at Rp1,350 it is 1.64x today's fundamental of Rp821 and the Rp3,000 ceiling is 3.7x. Spending up to Rp2tn (about US$110m, 3.6% of fundamental equity) at those prices transfers value from continuing holders, and the model includes neither the cash outflow nor the count cut, so neutrality is an unmodelled assumption.
challenges.answer: The value-neutral wording is removed. Section 3 states the treasury-asset treatment (count flat, no cash-out line because execution is undisclosed) and the per-share effect: about Rp3 of value transferred at Rp1,350 and about Rp14 at the Rp3,000 ceiling. The report now says the programme is only neutral at fundamental value, which the current price exceeds.

challenges.challenge: The tax rate is 14.5% while the 9M LK effective rate is 3.5% (US$14.148m on US$409.074m), because Q3 booked roughly a US$48.7m benefit (H1 tax US$62.8m). That benefit is never explained; if it reflects a recurring incentive or final-tax mix, the forward rate is 11pp too high and value is materially understated.
challenges.answer: Note 38 reconciles the charge: nine-month current tax US$12.514m plus deferred US$1.634m equals US$14.148m on PBT US$409.074m, a 3.5% effective rate; the parent carries a US$250.207m fiscal loss and a US$65.626m tax-facility benefit, while subsidiaries pay final tax. The forward rate now starts at 3.5% and steps to 18% by FY2030E as the losses are consumed; the H1 14.5% is identified as inflated by the Q3 deferred reversal.

challenges.challenge: The bull's +4pp revenue growth is applied to every forecast year and compounds to about 7% a year for a decade, yet capex is capped at 4% of revenue and the bull narrative is wider spreads, not new volume. That shock, not the base margin, drives the bull to US$2,306 (2.4x the base 733) and supplies about US$393 of the probability-weighted US$943; as a one-year or realisation shock the bull, and the target, would be much lower.
challenges.answer: The bull is now a realisation shock, not a volume shock: revenue growth carries no bull add (zero) and gross margin adds five points, mirrored by a bear that takes five points off margin with zero revenue add. On the current run the business bull DCF is Rp2,493.7 and its twelve-month bull value is Rp2,862.7, the base Rp1,261.1, the bear zero, the weighted fundamental Rp1,346.2 and the target Rp1,489.3. The report explains that capacity and capex are fixed, so a compounding revenue add was inconsistent with the narrative.

challenges.challenge: The US$62.6m inventory allowance that carries the spread-not-write-down conclusion could not be located in the archived S17 text, and the 2027-03-31 catalyst is cited to S17, which dates neither the audited FY2026 results nor the CA-EDC start (S5 carries the Q1 2027 start).
challenges.answer: The allowance is located in Note 8, page 91 of S17: US$62.623m at 30 Sep 2026 and US$62.623m at 31 Dec 2025, fact F84, and the report cites it. The March 2027 catalyst is now cited to S5 for the CA-EDC Q1 2027 start; the audited-results timing is no longer attributed to S17.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis — cash flow and capex
challenges.challenge: Section 3 says "the operating business funded capex", but the placeholders in the same sentence resolve to nine-month operating cash flow of US$378.9m (F69) against PP&E acquisitions of US$572.5m (F68) — about 66 per cent — and operating cash flow before the US$476.7m inventory release is about -US$97.8m. The funding claim is false on the report's own numbers.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now sets nine-month PP&E acquisitions against operating cash flow of the same period, states that the operating business did not fund capex, and that operating cash flow was negative before the inventory release (inventories fell from the opening to the closing balance). No model change.

challenges.challenge: The two-part SOTP direction claim is not reproducible and is inverted. The base DCF of Rp1,099 already carries 60 per cent of CDIA at its fundamental (Rp119.51). Re-marking that stake at CDIA's house target (Rp286.60) raises TPIA equity by about US$690m, or about Rp145 a share, to about Rp1,244 — above the base, not below it; at CDIA's Rp362 market price it is higher again (about Rp1,309). A lower result requires an inconsistent construction that deducts the 40 per cent minority at the target and then adds the 60 per cent at the target, counting the premium twice.
challenges.answer: The inverted two-part SOTP claim is removed. Section 4 now states that the base DCF carries the parent 60 per cent stake at CDIA fundamental, and presents the CDIA marks as a sensitivity on the 40 per cent minority. It states the correct direction: a consistent re-mark of the parent stake at CDIA house target or market price raises TPIA equity above the base, because the owned stake is an asset while the minority deduction is unchanged; a fall requires re-marking the minority but not the parent stake, which double-counts the premium. No model change.

challenges.section: fund record qc_justifications.konglo.overlay; review record C13
challenges.challenge: The konglo overlay justification is stale: it quotes 1.16x, a target of Rp1,486 and a twelve-month fundamental of Rp1,337, while the current run is 1.1508x, base regime target Rp1,485.4 and twelve-month fundamental Rp1,346.3. Review response C13 calls the bull twelve-month value Rp2,494, which is the bull v0 (Rp2,493.8); the current twelve-month bull is Rp2,862.8.
challenges.answer: The konglo overlay justification is refreshed to the current run: price 1.1509x fundamental, base regime target Rp1,485.4, twelve-month fundamental Rp1,346.2, target Rp1,489.3, with the three regime targets. C13 now distinguishes the business bull DCF (Rp2,493.7) from the twelve-month bull value (Rp2,862.7).

challenges.challenge: About fifteen figures are spelled out in prose instead of placeholders — for example "sixty point five per cent", "eleven point seven per cent", "seventy-eight point four per cent", "sixteen point seven per cent", "about three hundred and twenty-nine million dollars", "one hundred and forty-five million", "three hundred and sixteen million", "roughly three rupiah ... roughly fourteen", "about six times EBITDA and about eight times earnings", "roughly seven per cent higher", "sixty per cent", "four-fifths", "twelve per cent" and "seventy-four per cent". The digit-based lint passes while these will not re-resolve when the model changes.
challenges.answer: All the listed spell-outs are replaced with placeholders or facts: growth and decline percentages removed in favour of the underlying F-facts, peer medians replaced by a placeholder-based comparison, the CDIA dollar marks replaced by the F-facts and a direction-only statement, per-share buyback transfers described without numerals, and the oil-link shares and controller stake expressed through placeholders. The report is now 3,477 words and every figure re-resolves.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 attributes the FY2025A EBITDA loss to "the enlarged base carries full-year depreciation". Depreciation does not enter EBITDA, and Aster was consolidated only from mid-2025, so the explanation is wrong twice over. The loss is the trough spread: the S17 nine-month 2025 comparative shows revenue of US$5,102.4m against raw materials and manufacturing of US$5,135.5m, a gross loss of about US$33.1m.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now attributes the FY2025A EBITDA loss to the trough spread, not depreciation: the prior-year nine-month comparative shows revenue of US$5,102.4m against raw materials and manufacturing of US$5,135.5m (fact F88), a gross loss, with Aster consolidated only from mid-2025. The negative-EBITDA fact is unchanged.

missing_bull_case.note: CA-EDC's US$800m project gets only the generic +3% revenue growth and Phase II (~US$1bn) is excluded with no sourced contribution, so the project is effectively valued at zero; the US$75 long-run Brent anchor NAV is asserted but never quantified; no SOTP cross-check marks the covered CDIA stake at house value, even though the bridge itself uses CDIA's fundamental.

missing_bear_case.note: No current maturities (US$768m of bank loans, bonds and leases inside 12 months, F44-F47) and no interest cover (about 2.5x FY2026E: EBITDA US$948m / finance cost US$374m); Q3 operating EBITDA was -US$6.5m and Q3 attributable profit -US$3.4m; 9M CFO of US$378.9m rests on a US$476.7m inventory release.

assumption_realism.note: The 16.0% base margin is a calibration identity that reproduces the 9M 11.7% at the period's US$97 Brent, not an independent through-cycle estimate, and both the 9M window and the FY2022-25 history are downcycle; the bull's +4pp revenue growth compounds to about 7% a year for a decade against capex capped at 4% of revenue.

evidence_and_citations.note: The bridge is not rolled despite the update's premise: investment in associates is US$174.8m against the LK's 30 Sep US$210.956m (Note 11), and the CDIA NCI is the 30 June US$468.395m (F42) against the LK's 30 Sep US$473.866m (Note 31). The US$62.6m inventory allowance could not be located in the archived S17 text, and the 31 Mar 2027 catalyst is cited to S17, which dates neither the audit nor CA-EDC.

valuation_method_fit.note: The engine's market.bs_date is 2026-06-30, so FY2026E FCFF is counted at 50.4% from 1 July while the bridge uses 30 Sep net debt, double-counting Q3; the CDIA minority mark is one of four plausible marks and only one is shown; the konglo walk never presents the three regime targets and gives no TPIA-specific reason for 30% closure.

bias_and_tone.note: Section 4 calls the target the base regime case although the base regime value is 1,336, below the 1,350 price; the 1.1% HOLD return depends on the 25% bull regime in which the premium expands 15%; the buyback is called value-neutral at 1.64x today's fundamental and the balance-sheet roll is called a trim at the margin when it cuts about US$334m, near 5% of the target.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model's Brent path is the deck's yearly series (96, 84, 80, 78, 76.5, then 84.46 by FY2035E), so the US$75 long-run anchor quoted in sections 2 and 4 is never actually used and the anchor-75 value is not shown; the cost link itself is applied consistently across forecast years.

conservatism_audit.note: Tax is set at 14.5% against the 9M LK effective 3.5% (a roughly US$48.7m Q3 benefit left unexplained); the oil link is cost-only with no crack offset for the integrated refinery; NWC is held at the released 9.9% rather than the H1 12.8%, so the working-capital release is capitalised; the Rp2tn buyback cash out is not in the cash path.

calibration.note: The BLOCK gate is justified for a transition year, but its anchor FY2025A (revenue US$7,000m, EBITDA -US$389.2m) is unverified pack data whose negative EBITDA cannot be explained by full-year depreciation, and FY2026E EBITDA of US$947.7m (8.6%) sits below the 9M actual operating EBITDA margin of 12.2% because Q4 is assumed at the Q3 loss run-rate without disclosure.

signoff.notes: APPROVED (round 2) — ADD, target Rp1,489.3, TR +10.9%; leave at signoff for the Director to publish; the stage is not advanced by me. The round-1 return is answered on substance, and nothing in the QC round-2 list or my own read moves the rating, the target or the thesis. VERIFIED. L1-L5 are fixed and checked: section 3 now measures nine-month operating cash flow of US$378.9m against PP&E acquisitions of US$572.5m and says the operating business did not fund capex (cash flow about -US$97.8m before the US$476.7m inventory release); the inverted two-part SOTP claim is gone and the direction is now correct (a consistent re-mark of the 60% CDIA stake raises TPIA equity); the konglo overlay justification reads 1.1509x, base regime Rp1,485.4, fundamental Rp1,346.2, target Rp1,489.3, and C13 separates the bull DCF Rp2,493.7 from the twelve-month bull Rp2,862.7; the spelled-out numerals are replaced (3,481 words, lint PASS); and the FY2025A EBITDA loss is attributed to the trough spread (9M-2025 revenue US$5,102.4m against materials US$5,135.5m, F88), not depreciation. The arithmetic reproduces: the twelve-month fundamental Rp1,346.2 is 50% x Rp1,261.1 + 25% x zero + 25% x Rp2,862.7; the target is Rp1,346.2 x the 1.106 premium kept = Rp1,489.3; the total return is (1,489.3 + 8) / 1,350 - 1 = 10.9%, ADD under fund rules (add_min 10.0, buy_min 25.0). METHOD. VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL: through-cycle FCFF DCF on the deck's Brent path, not spot; a mid-cycle 17.5% base-input margin bracketed by the nine-month trough (11.7%) and the clean H1 (16.7%) with both observations sourced; the oil link stated as cost-side only, with the crack credit refused for want of a series; working capital rebuilt to the H1 12.8% from FY2027E; other gains excluded from the base; CA-EDC Phase I inside the DCF and pre-FID Phase II excluded. MOST_LIKELY: FY2026E anchors the nine-month actual with Q4 at the Q3 run-rate (the cautious end, disclosed), scenarios are mirrored +/-5pp gross-margin shocks with zero revenue-growth shock on 50/25/25 probabilities, no buyback accretion, no default haircut. The bear at zero is a debt-and-minority subordination case at a trough spread, not an assumed default, and is described that way; it is a hard downside but it makes the ADD conservative, not the reverse. KONGLO AND GROUP.
